newsitem.title: USA: PairGain slides further on price worries.
newsitem.headline: PairGain slides further on price worries.

text.p: PairGain Technologies shares skidded for the second straight day as market sources cited continued concern about comments made at an investor conference Thursday regarding possible price competition.
The share closed down 1-7/8 at 20-1/2 and was the fifth most actively traded issue on the Nasdaq market, with nearly 10 million shares changing hands. The share closed at 26 on Wednesday.
Market sources cited investor concern after the company said in a presentation to a Hambrecht & Quist technology conference Thursday it could see competitive pricing pressure.
PairGain CEO Charles Strauch was not immediately available for comment on Friday. The share traded as high as 42-1/2 in January.

H&Q analyst Joe Noel was not available for comment on Friday, but said at the end of the conference on Thursday that PairGain had repeated previous comments in its presentation. Noel, who had chosen the stock earlier in the week as his pick of the conference, said he thought market concerns over pricing was overdone.
"I think the competitive situation of PairGain has changed only on the margin," he told investors in a conference wrap-up session. "The pricing pressures are greatly overblown."

Tustin, Calif.-based PairGain produces a line of products which allows telephone companies and owners of private networks to transmit high-speed data over ordinary coper wires with the same quality previously only available over fiber optics.
